stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding is earmarked for co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas increasingly critical to national defense. With the DoD's focus on these capabilities, True Anomaly's timing couldn't be better.
stories.soWhat: In a market where cash often trumps genuine innovation, True Anomaly's funding is a reminder that the defense sector is still willing to bet big on perceived security needs.

stories.head: Space Force seeks to double its budget
stories.body: Lt. Gen. Douglas Schiess defended a plan to more than double the Space Force's budget, aiming for a staggering increase from $15 billion to nearly $30 billion. This proposal is indicative of a broader trend where space is finally being recognized as a key theater for military operations. The FY27 budget markup already added $1.4 billion for space resilience.
stories.soWhat: If money really does grow on trees in space, we're about to see a lot more branches sprouting in defense budgets.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant passes design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has cleared its critical design review, a significant milestone for the program. This development comes amid rising interest in reusable spacecraft, as the military seeks more affordable access to orbit. The clock is now ticking for actual flight tests.
stories.soWhat: Passing a design review is like getting a gold star in school; it looks good on paper, but we still need to see if it can actually deliver when the bell rings.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With significant funding secured, True Anomaly's strategy for deploying its capital will be crucial in shaping the co-orbital security landscape.

watchlist.title: Watch for Space Force's budget negotiations
watchlist.body: As the Space Force pushes for a budget increase, the outcomes of these negotiations could set the tone for future defense spending in space.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's flight schedule is critical now
watchlist.body: With the design review passed, all eyes will be on Sierra Space to deliver on timelines for the Dream Chaser's first flight tests.

watchlist.title: Anticipate more defense-tech IPOs
watchlist.body: The recent buzz around the defense-tech IPO window suggests that more companies may look to go public, potentially reshaping investment dynamics in the sector.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
